title: How to select layers with keyboard in Figma on Mac: Enter, Tab and Option Space steps
metaTitle: Select Layers with Keyboard in Figma on Mac: Step by Step
description: How to select layers with keyboard in Figma on Mac: Enter, Shift+Enter, Tab and Option+Space, plus box select and common fixes.
targetKeyword: how to select layers with keyboard in figma on mac
intro: To select a layer with the keyboard in Figma on Mac, select its parent frame or group first, then press Enter to pick a child layer. Press Shift+Enter to move back up to the parent, and Tab or Shift+Tab to move between siblings.
tldr: Enter moves down into a child layer. Shift+Enter moves back up to the parent.
Tab and Shift+Tab move between sibling layers at the same level.
Option Space starts keyboard box select. Arrow keys move the pink cursor, Return selects, Esc closes.
Option Command A selects matching layers. Command A selects all. Command Shift A inverts the selection.
If Option Command A does nothing, restart Figma and check for a conflicting macOS shortcut.

blocks.text: Before you start: how keyboard selection works in Figma

Figma's keyboard controls are on by default. Figma says you cannot switch them off, so there is no setting to find. You do not need a plugin either. Open a file in the Figma desktop app on your Mac and the keys work.

Keyboard selection is a tree walk. A file holds frames, frames hold groups, and groups hold shapes and text. Enter moves down the tree, Shift+Enter moves up, and Tab moves across the branch you are in. Each key press changes the selection, so watch the outline after every press.
Some tasks still need a mouse or trackpad. Figma's help article says some functionality can only be done that way. Keep your trackpad nearby for drawing, resizing and anything the keys skip.
Why keyboard selection matters to more people than you expect

The CDC reports that more than 1 in 4 US adults, over 70 million people, had a disability in 2022. Keyboard access matters for a large group of people. Learning Figma's keyboard support is worth the time, even if you have never needed it.

A 2013 WebAIM survey collected 216 valid responses from people with low vision. Of those, 47.5% said they always or often use a keyboard to navigate web pages. That survey covers websites, not Figma, so treat it as background, not as a Figma figure.
Select a child layer and move between siblings
Most keyboard selection starts with a parent. Click a frame or group first. Press Enter to step down into its children. Press Tab to move sideways to the next layer in the same parent.

Siblings are layers that share a parent. In a card, the image, title and body text are siblings. Tab moves through them one at a time, and Shift+Tab goes back. Tab never leaves the parent, so you still need Shift+Enter for that.
Worked example: select only the label inside a button
Say you have a card frame. Inside it sit an image, a title, a body text and a button group. The button group holds a background rectangle and a text label. You want the label, and nothing else.
Click the card frame. Press Enter to step into a child. Press Tab until the button group is selected, then press Enter to step inside it. Press Tab once more to move from the background to the label.
If you go one level too deep, press Shift+Enter to climb back to the button group. Then use Tab and Enter until the label is the only layer selected. Check the outline before you move on.
The common slip is pressing Tab on the card frame and expecting it to walk into the button. Tab only moves between siblings at the same level. Use Enter to go down and Shift+Enter to go up.
Box select from the keyboard with Option Space
Box select is for layers that are spread out. Press Option Space to start it. A pink cursor appears. Arrow keys move the cursor. Return or Enter selects what it covers. Esc closes the tool.
Box select also works with Command. Hold Command and press the arrow keys to draw a box. Keep holding Command to resize it. Dragging with the mouse while holding Command draws the same box.
Think before you press Return. Once you confirm, changing the set takes more keys. If the pick is wrong, press Esc and start again. Esc is a safe reset.
Select matching layers and select all with Command A
Option Command A selects matching layers. Select one layer first, then press the shortcut. Figma selects the other layers that match it. The toolbar has a button with the same name if the key fails.
Figma's slide deck article says this feature requires edit access. If you only have view access, the shortcut and the button will not work for you. Ask the file owner for edit access.
Command A is different. It selects all. Use Command A when you want every layer, and use Option Command A when you want every layer that matches one you picked. Mixing up the two is a common slip.
Invert the selection and clear it

Command Shift A inverts the selection. Layers that were selected become unselected, and the others become selected. Figma documents this in its slide deck article. Test it in a regular design file before you rely on it.
Esc clears the selection. It also closes box select. If you lose track of where you are in the tree, press Esc once and start again from the parent.
Find every shortcut in Figma's keyboard panel
Figma keeps a shortcuts panel. Click Help and resources in the bottom-right corner, then choose Keyboard shortcuts. On Mac, Control Shift ? opens the same panel.
Use the panel as a reference. Figma's pages do not always agree on every key, so check the panel when a key seems to behave differently from this guide.

blocks.text: What Figma's sources do not tell you

The sources behind this page do not name a Figma desktop version for these keys. The steps are not tied to a build number, so check them in your own copy of the app. If a key does nothing, the troubleshooting list covers the usual causes.

Desktop and browser differences for selection are not stated. The desktop app adds F6 and Control F6 to move between top-level areas of the interface. That is the only desktop-specific navigation key the sources list.
Shift+Enter appears on the Select layers and objects page, but not in the keyboard article. The steps include it because the first page documents it. Test it yourself to be sure.
Where the selection commands live in the menus

Some selection commands sit in menus. The slide deck article lists Main menu > Edit > Select all with. The options include Properties, Fill, Stroke, Effect, Text properties, Font, Instance and Variant. No shortcut is listed for that path.
Figma's help pages are not consistent about this. The Select layers and objects article places Select all with under Edit, but it also refers to File. If the item is missing, check both menus.
Option Command A does nothing: the usual cause
The most common complaint is that Option Command A does nothing. A Figma Community thread from July 2025 describes this on macOS Sequoia. The toolbar button worked, but the shortcut did not.

Figma staff suggested restarting Figma and checking for a system shortcut conflict. The original poster found a screen-capture app that used the same keys. Change or turn off that shortcut in the other app, then try again.
Mistakes people make with keyboard selection

items: Expecting arrow keys to move a layer. With nothing selected, arrow keys pan the canvas instead.
Using Tab to climb out of a group. Tab moves across siblings only. Use Shift+Enter to go up.
Mixing up Command A and Option Command A. One selects all, the other selects matching layers.
Pressing Return in box select before checking the pink cursor. Esc resets the tool without a selection.
Skipping the mouse for every task. Some functions still need a mouse or trackpad.

blocks.text: Make the keys stick: a short practice routine

Pick one frame with a few groups inside. Use Enter to go down, Shift+Enter to go up, and Tab to move across. Press Esc to reset whenever you lose your place. Repeat the walk until the keys feel automatic.
Then add box select. Draw a box with Option Space, then with Command and the arrow keys. Compare the two. Keep the method that feels faster for the layers you work on most.
What to do after your layers are selected

Selection is the first step in many jobs. You might group layers, add auto layout or turn a set of layers into a component. Read [how to add auto layout in Figma on Mac](/how-to/add-auto-layout-in-figma) or [how to create a component in Figma on Mac](/how-to/create-a-component-in-figma) next.

faq.question: Can I select layers in Figma on Mac without a mouse?
faq.answer: Mostly. Enter, Shift+Enter, Tab and Shift+Tab move through the layer tree, and Option Space starts box select. Figma says some functions still need a mouse or trackpad, so keep one close.

faq.question: What is the difference between Enter and Shift+Enter?
faq.answer: Enter moves down into a child layer. Shift+Enter moves up to the parent. Use Enter to dig into a group and Shift+Enter to back out of it.

faq.question: Is Option Command A the same as Command A?
faq.answer: No. Command A selects all. Option Command A selects matching layers, meaning the layers that match the one you picked. Figma documents both behaviors.

faq.question: Do I need edit access to select matching layers?
faq.answer: Yes, according to Figma's slide deck article. That article also says Shift-click and Command-click selection in the Layers panel require a full seat and edit access.

faq.question: Does keyboard selection work in the browser too?
faq.answer: Figma's accessibility page says its features work in a web browser, the desktop app and mobile apps. The sources do not say the selection keys differ by platform, so test them in the app you use.

faq.question: Where can I see every Figma shortcut?
faq.answer: Click Help and resources in the bottom-right corner, then choose Keyboard shortcuts. On Mac, Control Shift ? opens the same panel.

steps.name: Select a parent frame or group
steps.text: Start with a parent. Click a frame or group on the canvas, or click it in the Layers panel. The keys move from that point, so the parent is your starting place.
steps.tip: With nothing selected, the arrow keys pan the canvas instead of moving through layers.

steps.name: Press Enter to go down one level
steps.text: Press Enter to select a child layer inside your selection. Enter moves you one level down the layer tree each time you press it.
steps.tip: If the child is also a group, press Enter again to go one level deeper.

steps.name: Move between sibling layers with Tab
steps.text: Press Tab to move to the next sibling, which is the next layer at the same level inside the same parent. Press Shift+Tab to move back.
steps.tip: Tab does not climb out of a group. Use Shift+Enter for that.

steps.name: Press Shift+Enter to go up one level
steps.text: Press Shift+Enter to select the parent of the current layer. Use it when you went too deep and want the whole group back.
steps.tip: Figma's keyboard article does not list this key, but the Select layers and objects article does.

steps.name: Turn on keyboard box select
steps.text: Press Option and Space together. A pink cursor appears on the canvas. Move it with the arrow keys over the layers you want.
steps.tip: Press Esc at any time to close the tool without selecting anything.

steps.name: Confirm the box with Return
steps.text: Press Return or Enter to confirm the selection. The layers under the pink cursor become selected on the canvas.
steps.tip: If the selection is wrong, press Esc and start the box again.

steps.name: Draw a selection box with Command and arrows
steps.text: Hold Command and press the arrow keys to draw a selection box. Keep holding Command to resize the box. Dragging with the mouse while holding Command draws the same box.
steps.tip: Figma's help article says this works with both the keys and the mouse.

steps.name: Select matching layers
steps.text: Select one layer, then press Option Command A. Figma selects the layers that match it. The same action is a button in the toolbar, labelled Select matching layers. You need edit access to the file.
steps.tip: If the shortcut does nothing, click the toolbar button. A community thread says the button worked when the shortcut did not.

steps.name: Select all layers with Command A
steps.text: Press Command A to select all. Use this when you want every layer selected at once, then narrow the set with Shift+Enter or Esc.

steps.name: Invert the selection with Command Shift A
steps.text: Press Command Shift A to flip the selection. Layers that were selected become unselected, and the others become selected.
steps.tip: Figma documents this shortcut in the slide deck article, so test it in a regular design file first.

steps.name: Clear the selection with Esc
steps.text: Press Esc to deselect everything. It also closes the box select tool.
steps.tip: Use Esc as a reset when you lose track of where you are in the tree.

steps.name: Open the keyboard shortcuts panel
steps.text: Click Help and resources in the bottom-right corner, then select Keyboard shortcuts. On Mac, the shortcut for the panel is Control Shift ?.
steps.tip: Keep the panel open while you learn the keys, then close it.

troubleshooting.fix: Restart Figma and try again. Look for another app, such as a screen-capture tool, that uses the same keys, and change its shortcut. Or click the Select matching layers button in the toolbar, which the community thread says worked.

troubleshooting.problem: Arrow keys scroll the canvas instead of moving through layers
troubleshooting.fix: Nothing is selected. Click a frame or group, or select a layer in the Layers panel, then press Enter to step down.

troubleshooting.problem: Tab stops at the same level and will not go into a group
troubleshooting.fix: Tab only moves between siblings. Press Enter to go down into a group, and Shift+Enter to go back up.
The feature requires edit access. Ask the file owner for edit access, then try again. A view-only link will not allow it.

troubleshooting.problem: Shift+Enter does not select a parent
troubleshooting.fix: Check that your selection is actually a child layer. Figma's keyboard article does not list Shift+Enter, so confirm the key in the shortcuts panel.

troubleshooting.problem: Select all with is missing from the menu
troubleshooting.fix: Look under Edit in the Main menu first, then File. Figma's help pages are not consistent about where it sits.

lazur.spoken: Where is the Select matching layers button?
lazur.result: Lazur shows you the toolbar button on screen. You press the button or use the shortcut yourself, because Lazur does not press keys for you.

lazur.output: Lazur answers out loud and draws a circle and a label around the button on your screen. It does not click the button for you.
